newsitem.title: USA: Seagate sees weaker fourth quarter results.
newsitem.headline: Seagate sees weaker fourth quarter results.

text.p: Seagate Technology Inc., one of the nation's largest makers of computer disk drives, warned Monday earnings for the latest quarter would be below expectations due to weak demand for its high-performance disk drive products.

In a statement issued after markets closed, Seagate said revenues for its fourth quarter ended in June are expected to be 6 percent to 10 percent below the $2.5 billion reported for the third quarter ended in March. The company also said earnings before one-time charges could fall short of the third quarter's profit of $1.01 a share.

Wall Street analysts had expected the company to earn $1.06 a share in its fiscal fourth quarter, according to the First Call service. A year earlier, Seagate earned $101 million, or 92 cents a share, on revenues of $2.01 billion.

Shares of the Scotts Valley, Calif.-based disk drive maker have been under pressure in recent days on concerns about possible oversupply in the global disk-drive market. Last week, a Singapore newspaper reported Seagate may have to cut its high-end output in Singapore and that May and June production levels could be 30 percent below March levels.

A spokesman for Seagate was not immediatley available to elaborate on the reasons for the weaker outlook, but the company said in its statement that the long-term outlook for the storage business remains strong.

Separately, Seagate said it will seek authorisation from its board of directors to repurchase up to an additional $600 million worth of its stock. This is above the nearly $570 million of its stock purchased during the current fiscal year. At the end of its third quarter, Seagate had about 255.3 million shares outstanding.
Earlier, Segate shares closed at $42.375, up $1.75 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
